changelog: - **2FA recovery codes: minted at enrolment, shown once, spent once** (#1542). Turning on two-factor authentication had no way back: a user who lost their phone was locked out until somebody edited MySQL by hand, which is the real reason `require2fa` was frightening to switch on. Enabling 2FA now returns **ten single-use recovery codes** in that one response and never again — the new `TwoFactorRecoveryCode` table stores only `HMAC-SHA-256(NEXTAUTH_SECRET, '2fa-recovery:' + normalised code)`, because a ~38-bit code behind a bare digest is enumerable offline from a database dump, and bcrypt is deliberately avoided on the verify side (ten cost-12 comparisons per attempt is a DoS lever on the sign-in path; a work factor protects low-entropy human input, which CSPRNG output is not). At sign-in, a submission that is not a live TOTP code and is *shaped* like a recovery code is tried as one, timing-safe against every unused row, and consumed by a conditional `updateMany` (`where: { id, usedAt: null }`) so two tabs cannot both spend it. Rate limiting is two buckets rather than one: a failed recovery attempt is charged to the existing `totp` bucket (5/15min, so the second door is not a way to brute-force *around* the authenticator's limit) **and** to its own new `recovery` lockout stage (5/60min, so it does not *inherit* that allowance and a slow-paced guesser still runs out). A successful recovery sign-in writes `2fa.recovery_used` at `warning`, notifies the owner through the new essential-group `security.recoveryCodeUsed` event, and leaves `lastTotpStep` untouched so the TOTP replay floor (#865) is unaffected. `POST /api/account/2fa` gains `regenerate-codes` — deliberately *not* gated on a fresh authenticator code, since the person who needs it most is the one who just signed in with a recovery code — `disable` clears the set, `GET` reports remaining/total counts and never a code, and the account card shows the set once with copy/download plus a permanent remaining count. Impersonation is refused exactly as for the existing 2FA mutations. The format rules (unambiguous 27-character alphabet, dash-insensitive normalisation, and the shape test that keeps a 6-digit code out of the recovery bucket) live in the dependency-free `src/lib/recoveryCodeFormat.ts` under a 95% coverage floor; the sign-in-and-no-reuse promises are covered by `e2e/two-factor-recovery.spec.ts`. Design notes: `docs/two-factor-recovery.md`.

en: Turning on two-factor authentication now gives you ten recovery codes. Keep them somewhere safe — if you ever lose your authenticator app, one of them signs you in.
Each code works exactly once, the codes are shown only when they are created, and your account page always tells you how many are left and lets you generate a new set.
Signing in with a recovery code sends you a notification straight away, so you find out immediately if it was not you.
tr: İki faktörlü doğrulamayı açtığında artık on kurtarma kodu veriliyor. Güvenli bir yere sakla — doğrulayıcı uygulamanı kaybedersen bunlardan biri seni içeri alır.
Her kod yalnızca bir kez çalışır, kodlar sadece üretildikleri anda gösterilir ve hesap sayfan kaç kod kaldığını her zaman söyler, istediğinde yeni bir set üretir.
Kurtarma koduyla giriş yapıldığında sana hemen bildirim gider; bu sen değilsen anında haberin olur.
de: Wenn du die Zwei-Faktor-Authentifizierung aktivierst, bekommst du jetzt zehn Wiederherstellungscodes. Bewahre sie sicher auf — falls du deine Authenticator-App verlierst, bringt dich einer davon hinein.
Jeder Code funktioniert genau einmal, die Codes werden nur bei ihrer Erstellung angezeigt, und deine Kontoseite zeigt immer, wie viele noch übrig sind, und erzeugt auf Wunsch einen neuen Satz.
Eine Anmeldung mit einem Wiederherstellungscode löst sofort eine Benachrichtigung aus, damit du es umgehend erfährst, wenn das nicht du warst.
